newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly up in pre-report trade.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly up in pre-report trade.

text.p: Evening up ahead of Friday's USDA monthly cattle report started to dominate trade and CME live cattle futures closed mostly higher in light dealings, traders said . Feeder cattle ended up on short covering.
Live cattle closed 0.150 cent a lb higher to 0.025 lower with only February off at 63.200 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.450 to 0.150 cent higher with January up 0.375 at 65.750.

Nearby live cattle futures held in a narrow 0.200 cent range as many traders took to the sidelines to await the USDA's data on Friday. However, firmer boxed beef values at midday lent support to December, traders said.
Light bull spreading was cited on expectations USDA will indicate continued heavy placement of cattle into feedlots and in turn, increased fed cattle supplies lower.
However, some spreading of long February/short December was noted at the close, they said.

Estimates on the cattle report for feedlots of 1,000 head or more averaged 103.2 percent of a year ago for on-feed numbers in the seven key states as of December 1, ranging from 102 to 104.2 percent. November placement estimates averaged 105 percent in a range of 98 to 110 percent. Marketings estimates averaged 93.9 percent in a range of 91 to 98.
